title: Pick the Scenario

pairs.b: A broad, personalized mix for someone who hasn't said what they want yet
pairs.why: The homepage has the least context about intent, so it leans on the profile and variety.

pairs.b: Close alternatives to the item on screen: the user is comparing
pairs.why: Here the item on screen is the strongest context; substitutes help the comparison.

pairs.b: Things that go with what is already chosen, not substitutes for it
pairs.why: Showing alternatives in the cart can undo a decision; complements add to it.

pairs.b: The query states the intent; personalization only re-orders relevant matches
pairs.why: Relevance to the query comes first. Taste breaks ties, it doesn't override the request.

pairs.b: No live context, and it must earn the open: what's new since the last visit
pairs.why: An email is read later, out of session, so freshness and a reason to click matter most.

pairs.b: The episode just ended: pick the next thing while attention is still here
pairs.why: The just-finished item is the context, and the decision has to be made in seconds.

debrief: Homepage, product page, cart, search, email and end screen each have their own intent, constraints and definition of success. One algorithm for all of them leaves results on the table.
